original_question: Is it false that Sclerosteosis is caused by mutations in the SOST gene which affects the level of a member of the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) superfamily?

final_qi.question: Is it false that Sclerosteosis is caused by mutations in the SOST gene which affects the level of a member of the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) superfamily?
final_qi.long_answer: Sclerosteosis is indeed produced by loss-of-function mutations in the SOST gene, but the encoded protein sclerostin is a DAN-family Wnt inhibitor, not a tumor necrosis factor (TNF) superfamily member, nor is the disease mechanism centered on altering any TNF-family ligand or receptor. Therefore the claim that SOST mutations affect the level of a TNF-superfamily protein is incorrect, making the statement false.
